test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: From which country has the concept of Martial Law, which restricts Fundamental rights, borrowed?
solution:
The correct answer is **__The Uk.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Uk **has the **concept of Martial Law**, which **restricts Fundamental rights.**
 
• India incorporated the concept of martial law from English common law, although the term itself is not explicitly defined in the Constitution.
 
• Martial law denotes a scenario where civil administration is overseen by the military. This measure can be implemented in any region of India, typically during periods of insurgency, war, invasion, rebellion, riots, or other forms of violent unrest.
 
• Article 34 of the Indian Constitution outlines provisions for imposing restrictions on fundamental rights (FRs) while martial law is in effect.
 
• Additionally, Parliament is empowered to grant indemnity to government officials for actions taken to restore law and order during periods of martial law, even if such actions were in contravention of fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Martial law** entails the substitution of civilian government with military rule, accompanied by the suspension of regular civilian legal proceedings in favor of military authority.
 
• This state of affairs may persist for a predetermined duration or indefinitely, during which standard civil liberties may be curtailed.
 
• Martial law is typically invoked during periods of war, emergencies such as civil disturbances or natural calamities. In some cases, martial law may be declared following military coups d'état.
